boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations across downtown Northfield’s campus-adjacent corridors, each paired with one specific, sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Coffee in a Nostalgic Downtown Room
cards.subtitle: Division Street South corridor
cards.notes: Walk down Division Street South for an independent coffeehouse whose official site describes it as an inclusive community gathering spot.
cards.short_summary: A locally owned coffee stop in the downtown storefront district.
cards.evidence_claim: Goodbye Blue Monday is an independent, locally owned coffeehouse and community gathering spot at 319 Division Street South.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm before leaving because schedules can change.

cards.title: A Dessert Counter on Division
cards.subtitle: Division Street South corridor
cards.notes: Continue along Division Street South and scan the dessert case for cakes and pastries; the shop also advertises free Wi-Fi for customers.
cards.short_summary: A downtown bakery counter centered on custom cakes and desserts.
cards.evidence_claim: CakeWalk operates a custom-cake and dessert shop at 303 Division Street and advertises free Wi-Fi.
cards.source_title: Find Us | CakeWalk Custom Cakes & Dessert Bar
cards.access_notes: The business lists Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–6 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; holiday and event hours may differ.

cards.title: Books, Toys, and Puzzles in One Stop
cards.subtitle: Division Street South corridor
cards.notes: Browse the Division Street shelves for books, then check the store’s separate selection of games, puzzles, stationery, toys, and gifts.
cards.short_summary: An independent downtown bookstore with reading and play selections.
cards.evidence_claim: Content Bookstore at 314 Division Street is an independent bookstore and toy store offering books, games, puzzles, stationery, toys, and gifts.
cards.source_title: Content Bookstore | Northfield Area Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: The chamber listing provides current weekly hours, including a later Thursday closing; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Regional Art in the Guild Shop
cards.subtitle: Division Street South corridor
cards.notes: Step into the Division Street gallery building and browse the Guild Shop, which carries work made by more than 100 regional member artists.
cards.short_summary: A gallery, class venue, and artist-run shop in downtown Northfield.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield Arts Guild’s 304 Division Street facility contains galleries, classes, a gift shop, and offices; its shop features work by over 100 regional artists.
cards.access_notes: The Guild lists Tuesday–Friday noon–5 p.m. and Saturday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. for this facility.

cards.title: The 1876 Bank Raid Exhibit
cards.subtitle: Division Street South corridor
cards.notes: Follow Division Street South to the Scriver Building and examine the museum’s documented exhibit about the failed 1876 bank raid.
cards.short_summary: Local history exhibits inside the building targeted by the James-Younger Gang.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield History Center at 408 Division Street South presents a museum exhibit about the 1876 bank raid and grants free admission to students.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday 1–4 p.m.; students receive free admission.

cards.title: A Riverfront Pause Downtown
cards.subtitle: Bridge Square and Water Street corridor
cards.notes: Turn toward Bridge Square for benches beside the Cannon River; bring a device if the listed electrical outlets and internet would be useful.
cards.short_summary: A civic riverfront square equipped for sitting, picnicking, and connecting.
cards.evidence_claim: Bridge Square is a city park at 12 Bridge Square along the Cannon River with benches, electrical outlets, internet, picnic tables, and running water.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; improvement work or community events may temporarily affect access, so check the city project page if planning a group stop.

cards.entity_name: Northfield Arts Guild Water Street Studios
cards.title: Artist Studios by the River Blocks
cards.subtitle: Water Street South corridor
cards.notes: Cross to Water Street South and visit the Guild’s named studio building for artist workspaces, classes, a meeting room, and its own gift shop.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated Arts Guild studio and class building on Water Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield Arts Guild identifies Water Street Studios at 411 Water Street South as housing artist studios, a gift shop, classes, and meeting space.
cards.access_notes: The Guild lists Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–4 p.m. for Water Street Studios; classes or events may use separate schedules.

cards.title: A Community Stage on Third Street
cards.subtitle: Third Street West corridor
cards.notes: Head west on Third Street to check the Guild Theater calendar for plays, concerts, or classes before choosing a performance-day visit.
cards.short_summary: The Arts Guild’s separate downtown venue for theater and music.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield Arts Guild Theater at 411 Third Street West hosts theater productions, concerts, and classes; the Guild presents four theater productions annually.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled productions, concerts, and classes; consult the Guild calendar before walking over.

cards.title: A Civic Study Stop on Washington
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk along Washington Street to the city library for an indoor reading or study stop; check its calendar if you also want a public program.
cards.short_summary: Northfield’s municipal library in the downtown street grid.
cards.evidence_claim: Northfield Public Library is a city library located at 210 Washington Street, and the city identifies it as a public facility serving Northfield.
cards.access_notes: City information identifies the facility and address; consult the library’s current calendar or notices for public hours and program access.

cards.title: Picnic Tables and a Playground
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street East corridor
cards.notes: Follow Fourth Street East to Central Park and use its benches or picnic tables; the city also lists a playground and electrical outlets.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood-scale public square east of the downtown storefronts.
cards.evidence_claim: Central Park at 421 Fourth Street East provides benches, electrical outlets, picnic tables, a playground, and a portable toilet.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; the city has been evaluating playground improvements, so verify conditions if that amenity is central to your visit.
